title: Google's new image model Nano Banana 2.1 generates better images for less money
key_facts: Google released Nano Banana 2.1, an image generation and editing model, replacing Nano Banana 2 (February 2026).
It is built on Gemini 3.6 Flash; Nano Banana Pro likely remains Google's best image model.
A 1K image costs 3.36 cents, down from 6.70; a 4K image drops from 15.10 to 7.56 cents; Pro costs 13.40 cents per 1K image.
Google says it improves text rendering, character consistency, panoramas and infographics; handles up to 14 reference images.
Rolling out in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, AI Studio, Flow, Stitch, Google Ads and Gemini Enterprise Platform.
The older gemini-3.1-flash-image will be shut down on 29 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: Google is also cutting prices roughly in half compared with Nano Banana 2.
In practice, Nano Banana Pro often still produces noticeably better images.
Google will shut down the previous model, "gemini-3.1-flash-image," on October 29, 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: Image generation gets about half as expensive while Pro stays the quality leader.
notes: Quality claims are Google's; The Decoder notes Pro often still looks better.
